extracted.intended_audience: patent indexers / patent information specialists / examiners working with Derwent CPI chemical indexing
extracted.subtask_description: Assigning Derwent CPI chemical/activity/property/use codes (Parts P, Q, R, etc.) to patent documents describing compounds, compositions, formulations, processes, devices, diagnostics, and uses. Includes rules on applicability, cross-assignment, historic coding practice, and code-specific notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part P vs Part Q applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Part P codes are primarily applicable to CPI Sections B (Farmdoc) and C (Agdoc), and Part Q codes to Section E (Chemdoc). From 1981 forward, Part Q codes may also be assigned to patents that are only classified in Sections B and C, and Part P codes may be assigned to patents that are only classified in Section E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Part P for pharmaceutical/agricultural applications and Part Q for general chemical applications, but apply cross-assignments for post-1981 material as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediates coding rule (P vs Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part P codes are not assigned to inactive intermediates of active products. For example, a novel intermediate of an insect sterilant is not assigned P342 (“Insect sterilant”). Part Q codes, on the other hand, often indicate a broad field of use and are thus assigned in some cases to intermediates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assign P activity codes to inactive intermediates; consider Q: codes when the intermediate indicates a broader field of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Parts P and Q for retrieval of activity/property/use
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Parts P: and Q: are most useful for finding out if a known compound has a particular activity, property, or use, and for limiting the number of hits from structure searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching for compounds by activity/property/use, include relevant P: and Q: codes to narrow hits from structural searches; consider Manual Codes for more specific searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual Codes vs Chemical Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual Codes can often be used to search more specifically and comprehensively for activities, properties, and uses than the corresponding Chemical Codes, particularly in the area of general chemicals (Chemdoc - Section E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Manual Codes for detailed retrieval when available, especially for general chemical applications in Section E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadings applicability dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, codes are valid from 1993 for subs M0, M1, M2, and M6 and from 1981 for subs M3 and M4. Many sets specify their own applicability dates (e.g., Part Q codes generally applicable to M3 from 1970 and subs M1–M6 from 1981).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indexing or searching, respect subheading (M-code) applicability dates to avoid retrieving inapplicable historical references; OR older codes when needed per notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: P0: Use limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Set P0: are only used for agricultural (Section C - Agdoc) patents, in combination with P200, P210, P220, P241, P242, P330, P331, P340, P341, or P361.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use P0 codes for human/veterinary pharmaceutical patents; combine with specified P2/P3/P34 etc. as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: P003 exclusion for human/veterinary
rubrics_metrics.description: The code P003 (Contact) is not used for human or veterinary activities, and is therefore not used together with the code P001 (Human or veterinary activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid combinations of P003 with P001; follow the stated exclusion rule when assigning codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: P1 Plant Growth Media/Regulant structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset P1 covers 'Plant Growth Media, Regulant' including plant or soil use of steroids (P100), fertiliser (P11 with P111–P113), soil treatment/growth media (P12 with P121–P127), plant growth regulants (P13 with P130–P136), herbicide (P14 with P140–P145).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the most specific P1 subcode applicable (e.g., P142 Pre-emergence herbicide) and observe historical coding notes (e.g., pre-1981 assignments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on P14 historic coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to 1981, the codes P141, P142, and P143 were not in use; aquatic, pre-emergence, and post-emergence herbicides were assigned either P140, P144, or P145 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching older literature, OR the broader P14 codes to retrieve pre-1981 references that used different subs.

rubrics_metrics.name: P2 Antimicrobial/disinfection structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset P2 provides codes for antimicrobial/disinfection (P200 generic disclosure), antivirals (P21 with P210/P211), antibacterial (P220), antimycobacterial/antivenereal (P23 with P231–P233), antifungal/antialgal/antilichen (P24 with P241–P243).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use P200 for generic antimicrobials (particularly prior to 1981 where other subs used P220) and select specific P21/P22/P23 etc. where specific activity is disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: P21 antiviral historic note
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to 1981, P210 was assigned to all antivirals; from 1981 forward, P210 assigned to all antivirals that are not interferon-inducers (P211 assigned to interferon-inducers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indexing/searching across time, account for the shift in antiviral subcoding post-1981.

rubrics_metrics.name: P32 Anthelmintic and P32 notes
rubrics_metrics.description: P32 covers anthelmintic – general (P320), schistosomicide (P321), fasciolicide/distomicide (P322). Note: Nematocides are assigned P345, not a code in P32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflated nematocides with anthelmintics in P32; assign P345 for nematocides.

rubrics_metrics.name: P3 Other biocides and P33/P34 selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset P3 includes antifouling (P300), antiprotozoal (P31), antiparasitic (P33 with P330–P332) and other pesticide types in P34 (P340–P351 covering insecticide, insect sterilant, molluscicide, rodenticide, nematocide, lure/bait (P35), repellant (P36)). Codes in P33 are only used for substances that cannot be classified in previous subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the earliest applicable subset; use P33 only when prior subsets are not applicable; use P350/P351 historically for pheromones prior to 1981.

rubrics_metrics.name: P34 insect sterilant coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Insect sterilants are coded P342. Note that a novel intermediate of an insect sterilant is not assigned P342 if inactive (see intermediates rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign P342 where the disclosed compound itself functions as an insect sterilant; do not assign to inert intermediates.

rubrics_metrics.name: P4 Analgesic/anaesthetic/antiinflammatory/CNS structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset P4 contains analgesic/local anaesthetic (P41 with P411–P412), antiinflammatory (P42 with P420–P423), immunological (P43 with P430–P434), CNS depressants/tranquillisers (P44 with P440–P448), CNS stimulant (P45 with P450–P453). Many P4 codes include historical M5 applicability notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the most specific P4 subcode based on disclosed therapeutic/activity claims and take into account pre-1981 steroid coding exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: P5 Autonomic Nervous System and Cardiovascular coding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset P51 covers Autonomic nervous system activities (P510–P519 etc.); P52 covers Cardiovascular system activities (circulatory active, antiarrhythmic, vasodilator, etc.). Note: P520 or P522 are only assigned when there is not a more specific term for the disclosed activity, and general circulatory disease treatment is also indexed in P51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer specific cardiovascular subcodes over general ones; only use P520/P522 if no more specific subcode applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: P6 Metabolic (antidotes) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset P64 covers antidotes with subcodes P640–P646 (alcoholism treatment, antismoking, heavy metal antidote, pesticide/herbicide antidote, plant-protecting antidotes, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the precise antidote subcode when the antidotal use is disclosed; note 1981 applicability years for many subs.

rubrics_metrics.name: P7 Anabolic/kidney/liver/gastrointestinal mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: P71 Anabolic (P710–P714), P72 Kidney/liver active (P720–P723), P61 Antihormone/antimetabolite (P610–P617) and P62 Hormone active (P620–P625), P63 Cancer treatment/cytostat (P631–P634), P73 Gastrointestinal (P730–P738), P83 Diagnostic/analytical material (P831–P832). Notes include where food/feeds/additives are coded elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index appetite stimulants/gastrointestinal flora/animal growth promoters in P71 where applicable; otherwise use Q21/Q22 for food/feed-related compounds per notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: P84 Contraceptive coding and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: P84 covers contraceptives (P840–P843) including anti-implantation, antiovulatory and other contraceptives (including devices). Notes: prior to 1981 P610 was used instead of P841 or P842; insect sterilants are coded P342, not in P84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use P84 subs for contraceptive claims and avoid misassigning insect sterilant codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: P8 Blood/Respiratory/Misc descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: P81 covers blood activity codes (P810–P817), P82 respiratory (P820–P823). Notes: Pre-1981 steroids have particular coding (e.g., P820), so search P820 OR specific P821–P823 codes to retrieve steroid references from 1963.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include historical steroid codes when searching older records; pick the most specific blood/respiratory subcode available.

rubrics_metrics.name: P9 Skin/Dental/ENT/Mouth/Eye/Hair treatment mapping and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: P9 covers skin/dental/ear-nose-throat/mouth/eye/hair treatment with subgroups P91 (dental), P92 (ENT/mouth/eye), P94 (skin treatment with P940–P944 for wound, burn, other). Notes indicate cosmetics/perfumes/non-medical hair treatments coded in Q25 and skin protection in Q26; bandages/dressings are coded in R04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use P9 codes for cosmetic or non-medical hair treatments—use Q25/Q252; use R04 codes for bandages and dressings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part Q purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The codes in Part Q: are used to describe the activities, properties, and uses of a broad range of compounds and compositions, other than those coded in Part P: with pharmaceutical or agricultural applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Part Q codes for general chemical uses/properties across CPI sections A, D, E, F, G, H–M as mapped; do not duplicate P: pharmac/agro assignments unless cross-assigning per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q0 General use descriptor rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Set Q0 codes are only assigned when the use is not covered by a more specific code in Sets Q1 through Q6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Q0 only as a last resort; prefer specific Q1–Q6 subset codes if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1 Polymer descriptors and monomer exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Q110 assigned to polymer condensant or monomer; note: when a patent concerned with production of listed polymer condensants/monomers is coded in Section E, Q110 is assigned even if polymer use is not stated. Q12/Q13/Q14 cover polymer production/additives/processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Q110 for listed monomers/condensants in Section E patents even if use as monomer not explicitly stated; otherwise require explicit disclosure of use in most polymer cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q13 Polymer additives selection notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Additives are coded Q130 if no other code in Subset Q13 is applicable; additives coded Q130 are further defined elsewhere (e.g., flame retardants are Q130 and Q621). Additives to polymer surfaces are coded in Q13, not Q140, though prior to 1981 there was inconsistency (so Q140 should be OR'ed with Q13 codes for pre-1981 searches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer specific Q13 subs for polymer additives; for pre-1981 records OR Q140 with Q13 codes to ensure retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q140 Polymer processing notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Polymer modification and surface treatment of polymers are coded Q140 unless compounds coded Q132 or Q133 are used in the process. Depolymerisation processes and subsequent monomer recovery are coded Q110 and N153, not Q140.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Q140 for processing except when specific additive/process codes apply or when depolymerisation with monomer recovery is involved (use Q110/N153).

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2 Food/Cosmetics/Detergent descriptors and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Q21 covers human or animal foods (Q210–Q214), Q22 food additives/preservation (Q220–Q225), with notes that food additives are coded in Q22 not Q21; prior to 1981 different cross-codings applied (P710, R002, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Q22 for food additives, and consider historical cross-codes when searching older material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q23 Water treatment / Microbiology mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Q231 water treatment other than sewage/wastewater/pollution control, Q232 brewing/fermentation producing ethanol, Q233 microbiology lab culture/mutant formation. Notes: sewage/wastewater/pollution uses are coded Q437, not Q231; ethanol-producing fermentations combine Q232 with an N13 code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Q437 for sewage/wastewater/pollution control; for ethanol-producing fermentations assign Q232 plus N13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q25 Cosmetics/hair/perfume mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Q25 covers cosmetics/toiletries/hair treatment/perfume with subcodes Q250–Q254 (antiperspirant/deodorant Q251, non-medical hair treatment Q252, perfume Q253).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Q25 subs for cosmetic/non-medical hair/perfume applications; medical hair treatment uses may be in P93x/P930 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q26 Disinfection/skin protection mapping and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Q26 includes disinfection/sterilisation (Q261), skin protection other than sunscreen (Q262), sunscreening agent for skin (Q263). Notes: bandages/dressings coded R04; pre-1981 Section B or C disinfection used P200/P220; pharmaceutical/veterinary skin treatments coded P940 prior to 1981.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mix Q26 with R04 for bandages; use P200/P220 or P940 where historical coding dictates for pre-1981 records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3 Dye/textile/printing/photography descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Q31 covers dye-related descriptors (colour coupler Q311, organic dye Q312, dye assistant Q313, resist/discharge Q314, dye intermediate Q316, oxidative precursor Q317, non-oxidative precursor Q318). Q32 textiles; Q33 printing/coating/liquid crystals; Q34 photography/electrophotography descriptors with notes on pre-1981 photosensitive compound coding shifts to Q344/Q345/Q346.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the dye/photographic subcode most specific to the disclosed function and include additional Part W codes where applicable for certain dye types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4 CPI Sections H–M descriptors and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Q41 petroleum/fuels descriptors (liquid/gaseous/solid fuel and additives Q411–Q419), Q42 catalysis (Q421–Q423), Q43 chemical engineering descriptors (separation Q431, boiling Q432, refrigerant Q433 etc.) with notes on Q435/Q437/Q439 use and relationships to Part N codes (e.g., chemical analysis N102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Q4 subset appropriate to the CPI section of the patent; prefer Part N codes for laboratory chemical analysis/inspection processes introduced in 1981.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5 Chemical properties list and assignment principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Q5 lists chemical property uses and agents (acid/base acceptor, buffer, chelating agent, detecting agent/indicator Q505, ion exchange Q506, oxidising agent Q507, electrical insulation, magnetic material, odorant, optical bleach, plasticiser, solvent, surfactant, thermal material, tracer, viscosity modifier, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the most specific Q5 property code when the property/use is explicitly disclosed; many Q5 codes have M3/M4 applicability years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q6 Other properties/uses and indexing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Q6 contains miscellaneous properties and uses (Q60/Q61/Q62 and many subs Q600–Q624) with notes: stabilisers are indexed in Q62 not Q616; general chemical synergists assigned P863 not Q616; personal deodorants assigned Q604 and Q251; galenical additives in R3; U.V. absorbers for skin protection assigned Q263 not Q623. Historical shifts in thermal/sound insulator coding are noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the mapping notes for overlap (e.g., deodorants, stabilisers, UV absorbers) and use the recommended subset rather than generic Q6 codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part R scope and M6 applicability rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Part R codes cover pharmaceutical formulations, routes of administration, medical devices and diagnostics, additives, and packaging. Set R0 codes are applicable to M0–M5 from 1963 and M6 from 1976; sets R1–R7 apply to subheading M6 (from 1976 onwards unless otherwise specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use R: codes to describe important formulation features, devices, and packaging for patents coded with M6 (novel formulations/administration devices/formulation machines/packaging).

rubrics_metrics.name: R0 usage with M781/M782
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one of the codes in Set R0: is applied whenever M781 ('Use of one compound') or M782 ('Use of two or more compounds') is coded, i.e., for patents on compositions. Otherwise, Part R codes are only assigned if they describe an important feature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When M781/M782 is present, ensure R0 form-type code is added; for other patents, include R codes only when formulation/form is an important inventive feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: R0 Concept-shape mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Concepts describing shape or form searched with Part R0 codes are listed in the index and Chemical Code Dictionary. The applied code usually corresponds to the shape/form in which the compound is commercially used (e.g., emulsion paint coded R022 'Emulsion', not R043 'Film or sheet').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the R0 code matching the commercial or disclosed form/shape of the composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: R02 Liquid/semi-solid/gaseous/solid form mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: R02 covers liquid/semi-solid forms (R021 cream/paste, R022 emulsion, R023 solution/syrup, R024 suspension/dispersion). R01 gaseous forms (R011 aerosol etc.), R03 solid forms (capsule R031, tablet R038, microcapsule R033, etc.), R04 foams and other solid forms (bandage R041, film R043, prosthesis R046).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the most specific R0 form subcode based on disclosed dosage/formulation; follow notes about liquid crystal coding (Q33 together with R023/R032).

rubrics_metrics.name: R05 Timed-release formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: R05 includes timed-release formulation subcodes R051 (delayed release) and R052 (sustained release). Note: R051 and R052 are not searchable for general-use chemicals (Chemdoc - Section E) prior to 1981.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use R051/R052 for novel timed-release claims and account for searchability limitations in pre-1981 Chemdoc records.

rubrics_metrics.name: R1 General terms for galenicals and combination usage
rubrics_metrics.description: R1 contains general terms (novel dosage form R111, novel production R112, coated form R120, disposable R130, multicomponent R150, reference standard R160, special shape R170). Codes R111/R112 are used in combination with an R0 code for the particular dosage form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine R111/R112 with specific R0 dosage-form codes when indexing novel dosage forms or novel production methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: R2 Routes of pharmaceutical administration
rubrics_metrics.description: R2 lists administration routes with many subcodes (R200 buccal/sublingual, R210 topical, R220 implant, R231 injection, R232 infusion, R241 intraarterial, R242 intravenous, up to oral/rectal R280/R290 etc.). Transdermal searchable since 1983/Week 37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the specific R2 route code(s) disclosed; be mindful of searchable start dates for certain routes (e.g., transdermal).

rubrics_metrics.name: R3 Additives in formulations and coding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: R3 lists additives used in formulations (absorbent/adsorbent R301, accelerator R302, adhesive/binder R303, anticaking/disintegrant R304, buffer R305, chelating R306, coating R307, diluent/filler R308, dye R309, flavour R310, gelling agent R311, lubricant R312, plasticiser R313, propellant R314, stabiliser general/heat/oxidation/radiation R315–R318, surfactant R319, suspending agent R320). Additives are coded in M0–M5 and their uses coded in Part Q where the additive itself is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index additives both as ingredient codes (M-codes) and as R3 form/additive codes for M6/formulation patents; use Q codes to denote additive function where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: R4 Pharmaceutical administration devices and R46 syringes
rubrics_metrics.description: R4 covers administration devices (R410 catheter, R420 dosage into orifice, R430 implanting device, R440 inhalation device, R450 injection gun). R46 covers syringes and needles (R460 syringe general, R461 hypodermic, R462 remote control, R463 syringe needle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign device-specific R4/R46 codes when the device/form of administration is an important inventive element and coded under M6.

rubrics_metrics.name: R5 Processes; apparatuses; machines mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: R5 covers processes and apparatuses with R50 general (R501 physical, R502 chemical), R51 analytical/diagnostic/testing (R510 automated analysis, R511 chromatographic, R512 isotope detection, R513 spectroscopic/colorimetric, R514 other analysis), and many R52–R53 process subcodes (mixing, purification, microscopy, sampling, spraying, etc.). R501/R502 only used if not more specifically coded elsewhere in R5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the most specific R5 subcode available; use R501/R502 only as catch-alls when no specific subcode fits.

rubrics_metrics.name: R6 Diagnostic and analytical methods mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: R6 categorises material tested (R61 blood/plasma R611, urine R612, other body fluid R613, other material R614), reagents used (R62 antibody R621, antigen R622, color indicator R623, enzyme R624, fluorescent-labelled R625, isotopically labelled R626, other R627), and substances detected (R63 antibody R631, antigen R632, enzyme R633, drug R634, fat R635, microorganism R636, pesticide/agrochemical R637, protein R638, steroid R639, other R63x). Note: a substance detected is only coded R633 if no other code in Subset R63 is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code both the material/reagent and the substance detected with precise R6 subs, and avoid overgeneralisation where a specific R63 subcode applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R7 Packaging mapping and historical note
rubrics_metrics.description: R7 covers packaging (R700 aerosol can and valve, R710 ampoule, R720 bottle, R730 box/carton, R740 bag/blister pack, R750 cap/closure, R760 dispenser, R770 safety container). Prior to introduction of R7 codes in 1976, N101 was assigned to pharmaceutical packaging materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use R7 packaging codes for M6/packaging-related patents and consider N101 when searching pre-1976 records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steroid descriptors and code selection (intro to Part S/T/U)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following Part R, document introduces steroid descriptors (Parts S, T, U) and notes on code selection and format for steroids with detailed application examples and a steroid example. Notes on use of 'Exo' are provided in the steroid section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specialised steroid code selection rules in Parts S–U when indexing steroid-containing patents; consult the steroid example and exo notes for correct assignment.
